seidel_2018_detailed_kinetic_model.name: Detailed kinetic model
seidel_2018_detailed_kinetic_model.description: The detailed kinetic model describes methanol synthesis from hydrogen, carbon monoxide, and carbon dioxide over a commercial copper/zinc oxide/alumina catalyst. It predicts the rates of CO hydrogenation, CO₂ hydrogenation, and the reverse water-gas shift reaction from gas partial pressures and temperature. It uses a Langmuir–Hinshelwood framework built from elementary surface steps, with fast steps treated as quasi-equilibrated. The detailed kinetic formulation is steady-state and algebraic, rather than a dynamic model with evolving states. Its parameters were fitted to 140 steady-state experiments in a differential Micro-Berty reactor and its predictions were compared with those measurements; dynamic switching experiments in the paper were used for a separate model extension. The authors present the kinetics as a basis for modelling methanol reactors handling changing feed compositions, including for chemical energy storage.

seidel_2018_simplified_kinetic_model_ste.name: Simplified kinetic model, steady-state φ
seidel_2018_simplified_kinetic_model_ste.description: The simplified steady-state-φ model describes methanol synthesis from hydrogen and CO and/or CO₂ over a Cu/ZnO/Al₂O₃ catalyst, predicting reaction rates and gas composition. It uses lumped Langmuir–Hinshelwood kinetics and distinguishes oxidized and reduced catalyst surface centers, with their relative amounts calculated from an equilibrium morphology relation. The authors fitted its kinetic parameters to 140 steady-state experiments in a differential Micro-Berty reactor, spanning feeds from pure CO to pure CO₂. Dynamic feed-switching experiments were also used to assess the quasi-static surface-center calculation, although the model variant with dynamic surface-center changes described those transients better. The authors propose the models for methanol production under changing feed compositions, including chemical energy storage using renewable resources.

seidel_2018_simplified_kinetic_model_dyn.name: Simplified kinetic model, dynamic φ
seidel_2018_simplified_kinetic_model_dyn.description: This model describes methanol synthesis from hydrogen, carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide over a commercial copper/zinc oxide/alumina catalyst in a differential CSTR. It predicts gas composition and methanol production while tracking changes in the fraction of reduced catalyst surface centers, which affect the activity of the different reactions. The simplified model combines lumped Langmuir–Hinshelwood rate expressions and algebraic surface coverages with dynamic balances for the catalyst and reactor. It was fitted and tested against 140 steady-state experiments and feed-switching experiments reported by Vollbrecht (2007), using global optimization. The dynamic version reproduced the transient experiments better than a version with quasi-static catalyst states, and the simplified model fitted steady-state data almost as well as the detailed model while improving identifiability. The authors propose it for dynamic simulation and future design and control of methanol reactors for chemical energy storage under changing feed conditions; a 2020 corrigendum clarified the equations used.
